An important exception is a pioneering work by  Bernard Heyberger. This early study reconstructs how, departing from their  houses in cities such as Sayda and Tripoli, Jesuits and Capuchins visited  rural villages in Galilee and Lebanon. Inspired by the model of rural mis-  sions developed in Europe during the Catholic Reformation, their activities  hinged on confession and preaching. In line with the regional framework,  missionaries also carefully built ties with locals and offered their medical  competencies, which greatly helped their cause.?
